title: Second conditional and wish
titleVi: Câu điều kiện loại 2 và wish
summary: Diễn tả điều không có thật ở hiện tại và nuối tiếc — cấu trúc để đề xuất chính sách giả định trong Task 2.
whyItMatters: Để bàn về một giải pháp chưa tồn tại, bạn cần câu điều kiện loại 2: *If the state funded childcare, female participation would rise.* Đây là cấu trúc band 7.5+ dùng để mở rộng lập luận mà không khẳng định điều không có thật. `wish` thì xử lý phần nuối tiếc trong Speaking Part 3.

sections.heading: Second conditional: unreal present or future
body: The second conditional is **if + past simple, would + base verb**. It describes a situation that is imagined, unlikely or contrary to fact — in the present or the future, never the past.
*If I had more time, I would learn Japanese* does not mean I had time; it means I do not. The past form signals distance from reality, not distance in time.
This is why the second conditional is the natural structure for policy proposals that do not currently exist: *If governments taxed sugary drinks, consumption would fall.*

examples.right: If the state funded childcare, female participation would rise.
If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
If the city pedestrianised the old quarter, air quality would improve.
examples.note: A proposal that is not current policy.

sections.heading: was/were, could and might in the result clause
body: After **if** and **wish**, both **was** and **were** are acceptable, but **were** is the formal choice: *If I were the minister, I would...* In the fixed phrase **If I were you**, only **were** is standard.
The result clause can use **could** (= would be able to) or **might** (= maybe would) instead of **would**: *If she had a visa, she could attend the conference.*
Never put **would** in the **if** clause. *If I would have money* is a classic error that mixes the second and third conditional.

examples.right: If I were the minister, I would ring-fence the education budget.
examples.note: **were** — formal variant in a hypothetical role.

examples.right: If she had a visa, she could attend the conference.
If the library extended its hours, students might use it more.
examples.wrong: If the library would extend its hours, students might use it more.

sections.heading: wish + past simple: regret about the present
body: **wish + past simple** expresses a regret about a present state that you would like to be different: *I wish I spoke better English.*
The past form here does not refer to past time. *I wish I had a car* means I do not have one now.
**wish + could** handles ability: *I wish I could help you, but I'm abroad.* Use **could**, not **would**, when the subject of both clauses is the same.

examples.right: I wish I spoke better English.
I wish I could help you, but I'm abroad until Friday.
She wishes she lived closer to her family.
examples.wrong: She wishes she lives closer to her family.
examples.note: Sau **wish** dùng **past simple**, không dùng **present simple**.

sections.heading: wish + would and wish + had done
body: **wish + would** expresses impatience or a desire for a change, usually about someone else's behaviour: *I wish the council would fix the pavement.* It is not used about yourself (*I wish I would...* is wrong).
**wish + had + V3** expresses a regret about the past: *I wish I had applied for the scholarship.* This is the wish-counterpart of the third conditional.
For a neutral future hope, use **hope**, not **wish**: *I hope the application succeeds*, not *I wish the application succeeds*.

rows: I wish I had more free time.
I wish it would stop raining.
I wish I had studied medicine.
I hope you get the job.

sections.heading: Using hypotheticals in IELTS Task 2
body: Second conditionals let you evaluate a policy without claiming it exists: *If governments invested more in vocational training, youth unemployment would fall.*
They also support counter-arguments: *If this argument were correct, we would expect...* This move is highly valued at band 7.5 and above because it shows critical reasoning.
Keep the hypothetical consistent. Once you start with **if + past**, the result clause must use **would/could/might**, not **will**.

examples.right: If governments invested more in vocational training, youth unemployment would fall.
If this argument were correct, we would expect similar trends in comparable countries.
I wish more employers recognised vocational qualifications.
examples.note: Regret used as a soft policy critique.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I would have more money, I would travel.
commonMistakes.right: If I had more money, I would travel.
commonMistakes.why: Không dùng `would` trong mệnh đề `if`. Đây là lỗi kinh điển, thường do dịch trực tiếp từ 'nếu tôi sẽ có nhiều tiền'.
Sau `wish` diễn tả ước muốn hiện tại phải dùng `past simple` (hoặc `were`), không dùng `present simple`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I wish he will come to the meeting.
commonMistakes.right: I wish he would come to the meeting.
commonMistakes.why: Ước muốn ai đó thay đổi hành vi dùng `wish + would`, không dùng `will`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I wish I would have studied harder.
commonMistakes.right: I wish I had studied harder.
commonMistakes.why: Nuối tiếc về quá khứ dùng `wish + had + V3`, không dùng `would have`.
`Wish` không dùng cho hy vọng tương lai trung tính. Dùng `hope + present/future`.

ieltsTips: Dùng câu điều kiện loại 2 để đánh giá một chính sách giả định trong Task 2: `If the government invested in childcare, more women would return to work.`
Dùng `If this argument were correct, we would expect...` để phản biện — cấu trúc này thể hiện tư duy phản biện ở band 7.5+.
Trong Speaking Part 3, dùng `I wish + past` để trả lời câu hỏi về điều bạn muốn thay đổi, tự nhiên hơn nhiều so với `I want to change`.
Giữ nhất quán: đã mở đầu bằng `if + past` thì mệnh đề kết quả phải dùng `would/could/might`, không dùng `will`.

exercises.question: If the state ___ childcare, female participation would rise.
exercises.explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 2: **if + past simple**, mệnh đề kết quả dùng **would**.

exercises.question: Which sentence forms the second conditional correctly?
options: If I would have more money, I would travel.
If I had more money, I would travel.
If I have more money, I would travel.
If I had more money, I will travel.
exercises.explanation: Không dùng **would** trong mệnh đề **if**; kết quả phải là **would + V**.

exercises.question: I wish I ___ taller.
exercises.explanation: Ước muốn hiện tại không có thật → **wish + past simple**, dạng trang trọng là **were**.

exercises.question: I wish the council ___ the pavement outside our school.
exercises.explanation: Ước muốn ai đó thay đổi hành vi → **wish + would + V**.

exercises.question: Which sentence expresses a past regret?
options: I wish I had studied medicine.
I wish I could study medicine.
exercises.explanation: Nuối tiếc quá khứ → **wish + had + V3**.

exercises.question: If the city ___ (pedestrianise) the old quarter, air quality would improve.
exercises.explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 2 dùng **past simple** trong mệnh đề **if**.

exercises.question: I wish I ___ (can) help you, but I'm abroad until Friday.
exercises.explanation: Ước muốn về khả năng hiện tại → **wish + could**.

exercises.question: If she ___ (have) a visa, she could attend the conference.
exercises.explanation: Điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại → **had**, kết quả dùng **could**.

exercises.question: I wish I ___ (apply) for the scholarship last year.
exercises.explanation: Nuối tiếc về quá khứ → **wish + had + V3**.

exercises.question: If this argument ___ (be) correct, we would expect similar trends elsewhere.
exercises.explanation: Giả định không có thật → **were** (hoặc **was** trong văn nói); mệnh đề chính dùng **would**.
